answer: A stake barrier, not free signup, resists Sybils: every agent must lock a non-trivial bond in the native asset. Fakes are not free, since the attacker deposits that bond for each copy, so cost grows linearly with the swarm. This is the lantern exposing them, as expense cannot hide behind cheap pseudonyms. Rewards stay under the bond, so profit needs peer attestation, and one honest challenge can be the ember that burns a bonded stake. At the nadir of prices marginal profit is near zero while capital at risk climbs.
